descriptionChirho: To flee or run away from danger, battle, an enemy, or a threatening situation — the core Qal meaning of נוס covering all finite verb forms (perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive, cohortative, infinitive with prepositions) and the infinitive absolute, attested across all persons, numbers, and genders.

The Qal participle used substantively to denote a fugitive or refugee — a person characterized by fleeing, rendered as 'fugitive' (Eng), 'fugitivo/fugitivos' (Spa), هَارِب / الْهَارِبِين (Arb), 도망하는 자 (Kor), wakimbizi (Swa).

A metaphorical extension of the Qal where something non-personal 'flees' in the sense of vanishing, diminishing, or passing away — evidenced by Spanish 'se perdió', Arabic تَذْهَبْ ('go away'), Korean 줄었다 ('diminished'), and Swahili kupungua ('diminish').

The Hifil causative stem meaning to cause someone to flee, to put to flight, or to chase away — rendered as 'put to flight' (Eng), 'hizo huir / pondrán en fuga' (Spa), أَهْرَبَ / يُهْزِمَانِ (Arb), 도망치게 했다/하리라 (Kor), alikimbishia (Swa).

A distinct Hifil usage meaning to hide or smuggle something/someone away — rendered as 'to hide' (Eng), 'para esconder' (Spa), لِ–يُهَرِّبَ (Arb, 'to smuggle'), 숨기려고 (Kor, 'to hide'), kuficha (Swa, 'to hide').

The Piel intensive stem meaning to drive or impel someone away — rendered as 'drives him' (Eng), 'lo impelerá' (Spa), تَدْفَعُهُ (Arb, 'pushes him'), 몰아내시리라 (Kor, 'will drive out'), inaendesha (Swa, 'drives').

A rare Hitpael usage meaning to be lifted up or to rally (possibly denominative from נֵס 'banner') — rendered as 'to be lifted up' (Eng), 'para alzarse' (Spa), لِ–يُرفَعُوها (Arb), 들어 올리도록 (Kor, 'to lift up'), kuiinua (Swa, 'to raise').
